Class DefaultMailbox<T>

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.substrate.core.mailbox.DefaultMailbox<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of value delivered to this mailbox
All Implemented Interfaces:
Mailbox<T>
public class DefaultMailbox<T> extends Object implements Mailbox<T>
Default Mailbox handle: a single-slot drop box at a key, where each delivery replaces whatever was waiting.

  • Method Details

    • deliver

      public void deliver(T value)
      Description copied from interface: Mailbox
      Deliver a value to this mailbox. A mailbox can receive exactly one delivery in its lifetime — once delivered, the value is observable via Mailbox.subscribe() until the mailbox's TTL elapses or Mailbox.delete() is called.
      Specified by:
      deliver in interface Mailbox<T>
      Parameters:
      value - the value to deliver

    • delete

      public void delete()
      Description copied from interface: Mailbox
      Delete this mailbox, discarding any undelivered or unconsumed value. Subscribers that are currently waiting will be notified of the deletion. After deletion, subsequent calls to Mailbox.deliver(Object) will throw MailboxExpiredException.
      Specified by:
      delete in interface Mailbox<T>

    • subscribe

      public BlockingSubscription<T> subscribe()
      Description copied from interface: Mailbox
      Subscribe to the mailbox's single delivery. If the mailbox already has a delivered value when this method is called, the first next() call returns it immediately; otherwise the first next() blocks waiting for delivery. After the single value has been consumed, subsequent next() calls return NextResult.Completed (auto-transition from the underlying SingleShotHandoff).
      Specified by:
      subscribe in interface Mailbox<T>
      Returns:
      a blocking subscription that yields the delivered value and then completes

    • subscribe

      public Subscription subscribe(Subscriber<T> subscriber)
      Description copied from interface: Mailbox
      Callback subscribe with a ready-made Subscriber. The subscriber's onNext is invoked exactly once when the single delivery arrives. After the handler returns, the subscription naturally terminates via Completed and the feeder exits.
      Specified by:
      subscribe in interface Mailbox<T>
      Parameters:
      subscriber - the subscriber to deliver the mailbox value to
      Returns:
      a cancellable subscription handle

    • subscribe

      public Subscription subscribe(Consumer<SubscriberConfig<T>> customizer)
      Description copied from interface: Mailbox
      Callback subscribe with a SubscriberConfig customizer. onComplete fires after the delivered value is consumed by the handler; onExpiration fires if the mailbox's TTL elapses before delivery; onDelete fires if the mailbox is explicitly deleted before delivery.
      Specified by:
      subscribe in interface Mailbox<T>
      Parameters:
      customizer - lambda that configures the subscriber's handlers
      Returns:
      a cancellable subscription handle
